Analyst summary:
**What the supply‑graph tells us**

The downstream traversal from **BASF SE** (max‑tier = 2) returned two tiers of companies that could be affected by a disruption at BASF.  

| Tier | Companies with an SEC filing (i.e., we can query their own 10‑K/10‑Q etc.) |
|------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Tier 1** (direct downstream customers) | Cummins Inc.; Ford Motor Co.; General Motors Co.; Akzo Nobel NV; Avient Corporation; 3M Company; Corteva Inc.; Axalta Coating Systems Ltd. |
| **Tier 2** (customers of Tier‑1 firms) | TDK Corp.; ZF TRW Automotive Holdings Inc.; Mitsui & Co.; ENI SpA; NIO Inc.; American Axle & Manufacturing Holding Co.; Mobileye Global Inc.; POSCO Co.; Holley Performance Products Inc.; Brilliance China Automotive Holdings Ltd.; BP p.l.c.; Tesla Inc.; Toyota Motor Corp.; Chevron Corporation; BorgWarner Inc.; Harley‑Davidson Inc.; China Petroleum & Chemical Corporation; Romeo Power Inc.; Canoo Inc.; VinFast Auto Ltd.; Adient PLC; XPeng Inc.; Dow Inc.; Lucid Group, Inc.; Rio Tinto Group plc; Autoliv Inc.; Lordstown Motors Corp.; Exxon Mobil Corporation; Stanley Black & Decker Inc.; Garrett Motion Inc.; Komatsu Ltd.; Li Auto Inc.; Shell p.l.c.; Magna International Inc.; ArcelorMittal SA; Apple Inc. |
| **Companies without a filing** (no “get_supplier_info” possible) | The remaining ~150 companies in the list (e.g., Volkswagen, LG Chem, Nissan, many Chinese and Korean manufacturers, etc.). |

Only the firms labelled **“HAS a filing on record”** can be examined with `get_supplier_info`.  

**Evidence we were able to retrieve**

| Company | Tool(s) used | What was found |
|---------|--------------|----------------|
| **Ford Motor Co.** | `get_supplier_info` (10‑K for FY 2015, filed 11 Feb 2016) – also a targeted `search_corpus` query “BASF” limited to Ford | The filing contains the usual business description, risk factors, segment information, etc., but **does not mention BASF**, nor any disruption at BASF in 2016. The corpus search returned only older (2005‑2010) documents that also contain no reference to a BASF event in October 2016. |
| **General Motors Co.** | `get_supplier_info` (10‑K for FY 2015, filed 3 Feb 2016) – no targeted corpus search performed (turns exhausted) | The filing likewise provides the standard overview of GM’s operations and risk factors but **contains no reference to BASF**, nor any indication that a BASF disruption in October 2016 affected GM’s supply chain. |

**What we could not confirm**

* For all other Tier‑1 firms with filings (Cummins, Akzo Nobel, Avient, 3M, Corteva, Axalta) and for the many Tier‑2 firms that have filings (e.g., TDK, ZF TRW, POSCO, Tesla, Toyota, etc.) we **did not retrieve any documents** because our four‑turn budget was exhausted after gathering evidence on Ford and GM. Consequently there is **no direct filing or corpus evidence** linking those companies to the BASF disruption.

* For every company that lacks a filing (the large majority of Tier 1 and all Tier 2 “NO filing” entries) we were unable to obtain any SEC‑based statement at all, and an unfiltered `search_corpus` would have returned many unrelated matches. Therefore **no evidence**—positive or negative—exists in the data we examined for those firms.

* The traversal itself does not indicate *how severe* the impact on each downstream customer might be; it only shows structural connectivity (i.e., that they purchase chemicals, polymers, coatings, etc., from BASF). Without explicit disclosures of supply‑chain interruptions, the actual material effect remains unknown.

**Bottom‑line assessment**

| Affected tier | Companies we can say are **structurally at risk** |
|---------------|---------------------------------------------------|
| Tier 1 (direct downstream) | Cummins; Ford Motor; General Motors; Akzo Nobel; Avient; 3M; Corteva; Axalta Coating Systems (plus ~30 other Tier‑1 firms without filings). |
| Tier 2 (customers of Tier‑1) | TDK; ZF TRW; Mitsui; ENI; NIO; American Axle; Mobileye; POSCO; Holley; Brilliance China; BP; Tesla; Toyota; Chevron; BorgWarner; Harley‑Davidson; etc. (≈70 firms with filings, plus many more without). |

**Evidence status**

* **Ford Motor** – filing reviewed; no BASF mention → *no confirmed impact*.  
* **General Motors** – filing reviewed; no BASF mention → *no confirmed impact*.  
* All other listed companies – **no filing or corpus evidence retrieved** within the allowed turns → *impact unconfirmed*.

**What remains unknown**

* Whether any of the Tier‑1 or Tier‑2 firms actually reported supply‑chain disruptions, production delays, cost increases, or contract renegotiations linked to BASF’s October 2016 event.  
* The magnitude of any such impact (e.g., volume of chemicals sourced from BASF, financial hit, downstream knock‑on effects).  

**Conclusion**

The supply‑graph shows a **large network of automotive, chemical and industrial firms that could be exposed** to a disruption at BASF SE. However, within the limited evidence we were able to collect (Ford Motor and General Motors filings plus a targeted corpus search for Ford), **no company explicitly disclosed any effect from the BASF event of 17 Oct 2016**. For the majority of downstream customers—especially those without SEC filings—we lack any confirmatory documentation, so their exposure remains *unverified* at this time. Further investigation would require additional tool calls (e.g., filing retrieval for Cummins, Akzo Nobel, etc., and targeted corpus searches) to determine whether any of these firms publicly acknowledged the BASF disruption.
